prompt:
Find real, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports or pull requests as a burden (e.g. curl, Python, other projects). Cite the original posts and quote what they said.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.

response.content:
SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "The general trend so far in 2025 has been way more AI slop than ever before (about 20% of all submissions) as we have averaged in about two security report submissions per week. In early July, about 5% of the submissions in 2025 had turned out to be genuine vulnerabilities. The valid-rate has decreased significantly compared to previous years." | CLAIM: Curl’s maintainer says 2025 saw about 20% of security submissions become AI slop, with only ~5% turning out to be genuine vulnerabilities, showing a sharp drop in report quality and increased burden.

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "We need to reduce the amount of sand in the machine. We must do something to drastically reduce the temptation for users to submit low quality reports. Be it with AI or without AI." | CLAIM: The curl maintainer frames low-quality reports (including AI-generated ones) as harmful friction that must be reduced because they drain maintainer time and energy.

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "Every report thus engages 3-4 persons. Perhaps for 30 minutes, sometimes up to an hour or three. Each. I personally spend an insane amount of time on curl already, wasting three hours still leaves time for other things. My fellows however are not full time on curl. They might only have three hours per week for curl. Not to mention the emotional toll it takes to deal with these mind-numbing stupidities." | CLAIM: Handling a single low-quality/AI-slop security report consumes hours from multiple curl team members and causes emotional strain, which the maintainer identifies as a serious burden on volunteers.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "It is a little bit of abuse because most of these, that we call them AI slop, they’re just generated by someone really quickly. They don’t really understand it, they haven’t really verified it. The AI told them this is a problem, they pass it on to us. No effort, quick, easy for them and they just hand it over to us and we get a couple of hours of work per every such instance. It doesn’t work." | CLAIM: Daniel Stenberg calls AI-generated security reports “abuse” because submitters offload unverified AI output onto maintainers, costing hours of work per report.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "Previously, I mean two years ago, every such report, it actually meant that the reporter, if it had some kind of substance, it meant that the reporter actually spent some time thinking, testing, verifying. They actually invested something and then passed it on. And that made it, it was a built-in sort of balance to the whole thing. That balance is off now." | CLAIM: Stenberg argues AI tools have destroyed the natural quality filter that previously ensured reporters invested effort, leading to a flood of low-effort reports.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Curl project founder Daniel Stenberg is fed up with of the deluge of AI-generated \"slop\" bug reports and recently introduced a checkbox to screen low-effort submissions that are draining maintainers' time." | CLAIM: Curl’s founder publicly introduced screening measures because AI-generated bug reports were draining maintainers’ time.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Stenberg said the amount of time it takes project maintainers to triage each AI-assisted vulnerability report made via HackerOne, only for them to be deemed invalid, is tantamount to a DDoS attack on the project." | CLAIM: Curl’s maintainer compared the flood of AI-assisted invalid vulnerability reports to a DDoS attack because of the triage burden.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "\"We now ban every reporter instantly who submits reports we deem AI slop,\" Stenberg added. \"A threshold has been reached. We are effectively being DDoSed. If we could, we would charge them for this waste of our time.\"" | CLAIM: Curl resorted to instantly banning reporters of AI slop, explicitly calling the situation a DDoS-like waste of maintainer time.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "He went on to say that the project has never received a single valid bug report that was generated using AI, and their rate is increasing." | CLAIM: Curl’s maintainer stated that no AI-generated security report had ever been valid, while such reports were increasing, underscoring the burden without benefit.

SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2025/05/open-source-project-curl-is-sick-of-users-submitting-ai-slop-vulnerabilities/ | QUOTE: "“A threshold has been reached. We are effectively being DDoSed. If we could, we would charge them for this waste of our time,” wrote Daniel Stenberg, original author and lead of the curl project, on LinkedIn this week." | CLAIM: Curl’s lead publicly described AI-slop vulnerability reports as DDoS-level time-wasting that pushed the project past a threshold.

SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2025/05/open-source-project-curl-is-sick-of-users-submitting-ai-slop-vulnerabilities/ | QUOTE: "Stenberg, saying that he’s “had it” and is “putting my foot down on this craziness,” suggested that every suspected AI-generated HackerOne report will have its reporter asked to verify if they used AI to find the problem or generate the submission. If a report is deemed “AI slop,” the reporter will be banned. “We still have not seen a single valid security report done with AI help,” Stenberg wrote." | CLAIM: Curl’s maintainer publicly demanded AI-use disclosure for suspected AI reports, banned AI-slop submitters, and reiterated that AI-assisted security reports had never been valid.

SOURCE: https://lwn.net/Articles/1058266/ | QUOTE: "In the past, he estimated that one out of six reports turned out to be real security flaws. Now it is more like one out of 20 or 30. It is a total waste of the curl team's time and energy. The curl project is not alone in being besieged by AI slop reports, of course. Stenberg said that once he started talking loudly about the AI slop, he heard from many other projects that had the same problem." | CLAIM: Curl’s maintainer reported the valid-report rate collapsed from about 1 in 6 to 1 in 20–30, calling it a total waste of time, and noted many other open-source projects face the same AI-slop burden.

SOURCE: https://lwn.net/Articles/1058266/ | QUOTE: "Stenberg listed some of the things that he had tried to ensure that security reports were researched by a human. He added a submission form that required the reporter to declare if they had used AI. That worked for three or four reports, and then people stopped admitting to it. He tried banning reporters who used AI. That does not work well if the user can simply create a new account the next day. He tried public shaming, which worked to" | CLAIM: Curl tried multiple defenses (AI-use disclosure, bans, public shaming) against AI slop reports, showing the persistence and burden of the problem.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Python's Seth Larson also raised concerns about these AI slop reports back in December, saying that responding to them is expensive and time-consuming because on face value, they seem legitimate and must be investigated further by trained eyes before confirming that they are, in fact, bogus." | CLAIM: A Python security maintainer (Seth Larson) publicly warned that AI-slop security reports impose costly, time-consuming triage because they look legitimate but are bogus.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "\"Security reports that waste maintainers' time result in confusion, stress, frustration, and to top it off, a sense of isolation due to the secretive nature of security reports,\" Larson wrote. \"All of these feelings can add to burnout of likely highly trusted contributors to open source projects. \"In many ways, these low-quality reports should be treated as if they are malicious. Even if this is not their intent, the outcome is maintainers that are burnt out and more averse to legitimate security work.\"" | CLAIM: Python’s Seth Larson argued low-quality (AI) security reports cause maintainer burnout and should be treated like malicious attacks because they harm trusted contributors and discourage real security work.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Documented examples of AI-generated pull requests (as opposed to bug/vulnerability reports) being publicly described as a burden by open-source maintainers.
